Name: Torey Stevens
Badge: Joining a Conversation
What is one insight you gained from completing the Atwoodian Table yourself that might shape how you introduce it to students?:

I really liked that it has students examine the research to really understand what is being said on a topic BEFORE they form their own opinion on it. It matches up really well with layered writing/annotation. I've already begun to make changes to my research unit/projects for next year.

How does the Atwoodian Table idea compare to how you have taught argument and/or responding to multiple texts in the past?:
Instead of students finding sources to support their opinion, it helps for students to understand the topic before the form their own opinion.
What do you notice about the two sets of excerpts in this module (children in fancy restaurants and toddlers and technology)? How do the excerpts work together to invite students to join the conversation? What are some conversations related to topics you teach?:
They don't just give one side of the argument - it truly is joining a conversation. It allows them to form their own opinion (even a qualified one) rather than just siding with one side or the other. I use HMH into literature and Unit 1 really helps lend itself to this - I will be using this and layered writing when teaching unit 1 next year and the argument we write afterward.
